When the Government railways were directly under the control of the minister, although we had difficulty in getting cases against the railways settled, yet there was more satisfaction to be obtained than is possible now since the railways have been placed under the direction of a corporation. Before the railways were transferred from the direct control of the minister to this body, I must admit

we had some satisfaction, such as it was; but now there is no hope whatever for any man of small means to get a case settled against the railways. We have had considerable trouble along the Transcontinental railway for about a year now. It takes about three or four months to get any reply, and then a claim agent goes over the ground to ascertain whether the railway caused any damage or not, and finally the claimants are told: "No damage was done, and you may go ahead and sue if you want to." A great many people living along the railway line have not the means to sue the Government railways to recover their claims, and I promised some of my clients to bring the matter up before the minister, seeing that we have no other means of reaching the Railway Board than through the hon. gentleman himself.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Mr. Alward was the solicitor in charge of that work on the Intercolonial and Trancontinental and he is in that position still.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Well he ought to lose it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: As far as my information goes he is a good man. If I remember rightly he is a good Liberal too, at least he came from New Brunswick-

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Possibly a Unionist.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: No, I think he was appointed by the late Mr. Emmerson and he is a good man. I understand he is still in the same position and doing good work. He has, I think, been moved to Montreal. He was brought into the department by the late Mr. Emmerson and was promoted to Moncton by the late Mr. Cochrane. I understand he has now been promoted from Moncton to Montreal.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I understand my hon. friend to say that this gentleman is a law officer of the department and that he has been transferred from Moncton to Montreal?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Yes. I repeat, that as far as I know, Mr. Alward is a good man. I cannot understand why there should be so much delay when this work is all under the same officer.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Is he living in Montreal?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Yes he has been moved from Moncton.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
He is living rather far away from his field of operations.
105	-

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
I endorse absolutely
everything that has been said by my hon. friend from Madawaska (Mr. Michaud). In my own constituency merchants have merchandise sent to them over the Transcontinental railway. The Government for reasons not apparent to me have adopted a rather extraordinary way of running their railway through my county. They have stations, but in most cases no station agents, so that the freight is very often lost and consequently merchants are obliged to make claims to the railway. These claims have to be sent down to Moncton, at least that used to be the practice and from there they would be sent somewhere else. Very often we did not know where the claim was sent, but the Moncton people would say "We have received your claim and have sent it to the proper authorities to attend to." Weeks and months would elapse, very often over a year would intervene, and we would have no other news about the claim. That was the condition which existed up to very recently. I know, for I sent a claim to Moncton on behalf of one of my electors in Dorchester. That procedure is absolutely unbearable. If the minister were to say " Well, our staff is not sufficient, that is why we cannot give as good a service as we would like " the committee would, in a manner, understand; but all over the country-in every small centre as well as in every large centre-the Government employs a number of lawyers. Some lawyers are supposed to look after the Intercolonial railway, others are supposed to look after the Transcontinental railway, and still others are supposed to look after the Canadian Northern; the Government has so many lawyers that we really do not know to whom to apply. As an hon. member near me remarks, nearly every Conservative lawyer that we know of has something to do with the government railways in one form or another. I want to draw the minister's attention to another fact which has relation to this special item. A very great hardship for people-not only in my own district but, I think, all over the province-is that the special Order in Council which was to be passed to give legal existence to the famous corporation constituted to look after the whole system of Canadian railways has not yet been passed, if I am well informed. So that every railway which has been taken over by the Government has retained its separate and distinct entity-each is a separate and distinct organization. That is another conditions of things that ought to be changed. If I have a claim against the old



Quebec and Lake St. John railway, why should I have to see the officers of that company when the railway was taken over by the Government several years ago. And the Quebec and Lake St. John railway has a special lawyer in my city-I know him- and has other lawyers in the region through which the line passes. The same condition exists in connection with the Quebec and Saguenay railway, and with respect to every railway taken over by the Government. Why does not the Government resolve once for all, to run the national system on business lines? Why not group all these railways together and have one corporation? The minister has very often said in the House, "I cannot give information that is asked for because that information should be given by the corporation." But that corporation does not exist; it has no legal existence. For instance, what authority has Mr. Hanna to run the Canadian Northern railway? He has no authority from Parliament, and if Parliament did not give him authority, where could he get his authority from? There is no corporation created by law to enable Mr. Hanna and his associates to run the Canadian National railways. Every railway which has been taken over by the Government is still a separate organization. I do not think that is a business way of running things. It is no wonder we have deficits. In the matter of the legal department does the minister for one moment contend that it is a proper policy for the Government to retain all these lawyers acting for the different railways? In my own city, if we have a claim against the Intercolonial we have to go to one gentleman. If we have a claim against the Canadian Northern we have to go to another; and if we have a claim against the Transcontinental we have to go to a third. Is there any sense in that? Why not group all these railways together and have one or two lawyers in each large centre attending to railway matters, and not employ six or seven as is done now? There is absolutely no reason to have lawyers attached to the Department of Railways because the work is done by railway solicitors and not by these gentlemen. The minister mentioned Mr. Alward. I have not the pleasure of knowing that gentleman personally. I do not know whether he is responsible for the system existing at Moncton. If he is as efficient and competent as the minister has said he surely is not responsible, because from the way things were run at Moncton we could not get any satisfaction no matter how hard 
we tried; we would have to wait months for the settlement of claims for such small amounts as $15, $25 or $30. Sometimes over a year and a-half would elapse before repayment was made. I think the minister should give consideration to that special branch of his department because it needs plenty of reform.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: The hon. member has spoken of the loss of freight. I have had some experience with lost freight and overcharges in the case of different railways and I have never had to employ a lawyer to settle the claim. The railway companies generally have their claims agents and if the claim is good it is attended to. I think the minister might now make a statement as to whether there are claims on the national system of railways, and whether these claims agents are doing their duty. If every claims agent is doing his duty there should be no necessity for employing lawyers in such cases.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: The railways, of course, have their claims agents who go round settling these claims. There may be occasions when they might have to go to the courts, but as a rule these cases are all settled by freight .claims agents. The hon. member was talking about some land expropriations and also-

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: And even about freight claims of very small amounts.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Those claims go to the agent appointed especially to settle them. The hon. member asked why we did not consolidate all these subsidiary railways. That is impossible. The Canadian Pacific railway keeps alive all its subsidiary companies and operates them separately, as it were; for instance, the Quebec Central and the Kingston and Pembroke. It is the same with the Canadian National system. The railway the hon. gentleman mentions is part of the Canadian Northern system, although it is called the Quebec and Lake St. John. If judgments were obtained against that subsidiary line the Canadian Northern would of course be responsible.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Are there three boards of management, one for the Canadian Northern, one for the Intercolonial and one for the Transcontinental? I understand very well what the minister has stated regarding the Quebec Central railway, which is leased to the Canadian Pacific and is still administered by its own board. Are we to understand that for each of these Government railways there is a separate board?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: No. What I wished to convey was this. The Canadian Northern railway for instance has a board of directors, and for any subsidiary companies that form part of the Canadian Northern system the same board of directors is appointed. For the Intercolonial, the Transcontinental and the Hudson Bay railways of course there is no separate board of directors because they have always been owned by the Government. The hon. member will recollect that when the Bill was passed for the consolidating of the Canadian National system we excepted those three railways so that any bonds could be issued against them, The board of directors of the Canadian National system were appointed managers of those Government railways, and/ in that way they are treated as one system.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Now that we have had the legal aspect of the situation, probably we can get some information about the engineers. Quite a number of them are mentioned on page 96. Among all those engineers I am wondering whether I could find some one responsible for what has happened in the yards of the Transcontinental railway near St. Foy facing the Quebec bridge. A couple of years ago an artesian well was sunk there at considerable expense. A year or so afterwards some one dropped a big piece of steel into that well, with the result that its usefulness has been destroyed and the money expended is a total loss. I wonder if any one of these engineers could remove that piece of steel.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: The engineers mentioned on page 96 are not connected with railway work at all. Those now in the Railways and Canals Department are employed on engineering work in connection with navigation and highways. The engineer who dealt with this well at Chaudiere, as the hon. member stated would be connected with the Intercolonial railway. The engineers referred to in the Estimates are in the Inside Service.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Undoubtedly somebody must be responsible for the acts of other engineers even if they work in the Outside Service. If the mistake was made by some of the men working under these engineers, they should report to the department, and the minister ought to know what is happening.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: If the hon. member will give me some information I will make inquifies about the matter. I have not heard of it before.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
I did not think the
minister understood my question. I did not talk about Chaudiere at all, which is on the Intercolonial railway. I was speaking of St. Foy right opposite Quebec bridge on the main line of the Transcontinental. This artesian well was built to give the people on that side of the river a water supply. It was destroyed because it was part of the Transcontinental line, and the engineer even went so far as to sink a piece of steel in the well. Surely some one is responsible for this destruction.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I will make inquiries and get the information for my hon. friend.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I find thre is included in this list an assistant purchasing agent, a junior purchasing agent and senior supplies clerk. It certainly would indicate to my mind that there is a senior purchasing agent in charge of this branch of the service. Is there such an officer?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: We had a purchasing agent for the whole system, a Mr. Lavoie. When the Government took over the railway systems Mr. Lavoie was transferred to Toronto, and this is really the junior clerk. The Civil Service Commission gave him that title. Our purchases are now being made through a purchasing commission, but the services of a clerk are necessary in the preparation of the requisitions, and so on.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I find that there are two purchasing agents in the list, one at a salary of $2,520 and a junior purchasing agent at a salary of $1,925. Does it require two men to make out the requisitions for this department?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: It requires one man and another to assist him.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Then the name "purchasing agent" as given by the firm who classified the Civil Service would seem to be a misnomer. These officials are simply clerks.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: They have to understand purchasing, the nature of goods, and so on, in order to be able to prepare the requisitions and do the necessary work connected with the obtaining of supplies.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
Then they are merely requisition clerks, not purchasing agents. They fill out the requisitions for the requirements of one particular part of the service and pass them on to a purchasing commission in Toronto. If they are really purchasing agents, a salary of $2,520 would

be altogether too small. I find that a file clerk in this department receives a salary of $2,400. The work of a file clerk is of a routine character, and does not require very much brain power, ability or experience, but a capable purchasing agent can scarcely be obtained for the amount named in this item, $2,520. That is why I direct attention to the matter.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I agree with the hon. member that you could not get an expert purchasing agent for |2,520. But the duties of these officials are more of a clerical nature, although, as I say, they must understand the nature of the goods, the making of the requisitions, and so on.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
Are the requisitions
for the Canadian National Railways made out in the office at Ottawa?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: No, just for the canals now.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Then these two clerks do not requisition for the Canadian National railways?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: No, for the canals only.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: There is another item here with regard to which I would like some information. The Griffenhagen firm or whoever made the reclassification have apparently not been consistent in assigning salaries to employees doing to same work in different departments. lit the Interior Department, for instance, junior file clerks receive $615, $630, $660, whereas in the Department of Railways employees doing the same work are paid $1,300. File clerks in the Interior Department receive $1,005, $1,080 and $1,170, whereas in the Railway Department they receive $1,300. In the Interior Department senior file clerks receive $2,240 and $2,160 whereas the head file clerk in the Railway Department receives $2,400. Has the Minister any explanation to offer of the difference which exists in these cases?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
It was the Civil Ser

vice Commission and the officials of the department who took this matter up and arranged the salaries of these employees, I had nothing to do with it. For each of these positions, however, there is a minimum and a maximum salary, and some officials may have been longer in the service than others, which would result in a difference in the salaries paid. It is the first time it has been brought to my attention that the head file clerk in the Rail-

way Department receives a higher salary than an official doing the same work in the Department of the Interior. If the hon. member would like to get an explanation of the matter, it can be obtained from the Civil Service Commission, and I will make a note of it and, if he so desires, give him the information the next time the Railway Estimates come up.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
I appreciate the position that the minister finds himself in with regard to the question I asked and the impossibility of his giving a satisfactory answer to it. But does it not strike the minister that there is something wrong in the work done by the Civil Service Commission? That is to say, a file clerk in each department does similar work; there is not much difference in the quality of the work or the requirements for doing it. A file clerk merely files documents, and the same talent, the same ability, would be required to perform the same work in each department, sc that the salary for that class of work should be the same throughout the departments. No doubt one of the reasons why there is so much unrest and dissatisfaction amongst the civil service at present is because employees in one department find employees who are doing the same work in another department getting double the salary. I call the attention of the minister to this point, and I think it would be worth while inquiring into it for the general good of the Civil Service at Ottawa.
I understand the Railway Department is not going ahead with much new construction work during the coming year owing to the financial condition of the country. Why, then, does the minister require the services of these solicitors, a right-of-way agent and an assistant right-of-way agent? The services of these men might be dispensed with temporarily, if the department is not proceeding with the construction of new roads.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
We have a great deal
of work going on all the time in connection with the St. Lawrence canal, the Welland canal, and river work. There is plenty of work to keep these men going. When we were looking after the Intercolonial, we had a solicitor and his staff at Moncton doing work, but this work is entirely different from the work in connection with the canals.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
I want to draw to the attention of the minister a matter which will come up later under another item, but inasmuch as the minister has referred to the

fact that these engineers are mostly associated with the canals, I want to draw his attention to a matter of urgent importance. It is the case of the road around Hungry bay in the county of Beauharnois. The minister will remember an arrangement made between the Government and the county to maintain that road as a dyke, and the road was well maintained and kept in excellent shape until the outbreak of the war when we economised wherever we could. It appears that we have been economising to the extreme, because the reports that are coming to me now are that the road is breaking away into the muck and there is danger of the water washing through. Therefore, it is of urgent importance that the minister instruct his engineers to attend to this matter without delay.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
I will take the matter
up with the engineers to-morrow morning and see whether we have not provided something for repairs, and when my Estimates are taken up again, I shall be able to let the hon. member know just what the condition is.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I see the minister has four travelling auditors, two at $2,640 and two at $2,520 a year. As most of the work in connection with this department has been taken over by the Canadian National Railway Board at Toronto, there surely cannot be sufficient work to keep four travelling auditors busy in this department. The minister might explain why it if necessary to have these four gentlemen, and if his explanation is satisfactory, I will accept it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: These auditors are employed largely now in connection with highway work. The provinces receive grants from the $20,000,000 that was voted for highways, and we do not pay any accounts until our auditors have gone over them very carefully and certified that the expenditures are correct. They are really kept busy all the time even with that work. The Railway Department has also to audit the sums of money passing through the department between the Finance Department and the Canadian Northern and the Grand Trunk, as well as other expenditures in connection with the Railway Department. These men are, therefore, kept very busy.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
Do I understand the minister to say that accounts in connection with the Railway Department are first audited by auditors of the Railway Department and then sent to the Auditor General's Department where they are again audited? As
regards the amounts advanced to the provinces for highways, I under-
10 p.m. stand that the department send these auditors to the provinces to do the work. If the Dominion makes a grant of money to the different provinces, the least the provinces might do would be to send the accounts to Ottawa for audit, instead of the Federal department having to send auditors to the different provinces to audit these accounts.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
I hardly think that
would be possible. The hon. member will see that the provincial officers would have to bring to Ottawa all their books, vouchers and everything else connected with the transaction, so that it would be much cheaper and much more satisfactory for our auditors to go, say to Toronto or Quebec, and examine the books. In fact, the provinces probably would not let these documents out of their hands; and when our auditors go to the provinces, they are able to get the explanations from the provincial officials who understand the accounts. I think that is really the only way in which the work could be done. As. regards the other question, every account that passes through the Railway Department is audited by our officials before it goes to the Auditor General. Our auditors check up and audit all these accounts, and it saves a great deal of trouble to every one to have these men do the work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I understand there are two sets of auditors, those in the Department of Railways, and then the regular staff in the Auditor General's Department. I am satisfied with the explanation given by the minister. The minister, however, said that a good deal of the work of these auditors is in connection with grants by the Dominion Government for highways. These grants only commenced a few years ago. Are these four auditors new appointees, or have they been in the department for years, previously doing work in connection with the railways when the Government had full control of the Government railways?	.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: These men have been in the department for some years. When the Intercolonial was taken over by the management of the Canadian National Railway system, there was less work passing through the department, but the highway work came on at the same time and these men fell into that work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
Under the new condition of things created since the taking over

of all these railways and the establishment of the Canadian National Board at Toronto, what is the quantity and character of the work actually done by the department as regards railways?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: We have a good deal of work to do. There is a great deal of correspondence in the department in connection with the railways and, of course, we have control of all the canal work as heretofore.. Then there is work in connection with the accounts passing through the Finance Department and the Railways Department. These matters must all be looked into, and there is considerable correspondence in connection with them.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: If I understand the Minister rightly, the work is mostly clerical.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: It is more than that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Am I to understand from the minister that all the accounts coming from the different railways are sent to his department, and afterwards forwarded by his department to the Finance Department?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: No, we send our men out to audit the accounts.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Suppose the Canadian National Railways have spent $15,000,000 during a certain period. Has the Department of Railways, or have any of these officials whose salaries we are now voting, anything to do with that expenditure? Are returns made to the department? Do the department's auditors audit these accounts of the different railways?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
Parliament votes a
certain sum of money, and the items for which the money is voted are given in the Estimates. The Department of Railways follows these items and sees that the money is expended as Parliament provided. That is the duty of our auditors.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
The railways, according to the system which has been established, run for twelve months. Now, either they have a surplus or a deficit, as has been the case ever since the railways were taken over by the Government, at the end of that time. The amount to cover that deficit is supplied by a vote of Parliament. Is the Department of Railways kept informed every week or every month of the amount that is expended in excess of the amount provided by Parliament? For instance, did the minister know three or four months

after the opening of the year that the deficit on the railways was a certain amount, or was he kept in absolute ignorance until the end of the year?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: We know how the accounts stand from month to month. They are audited every month. The Finance Department will not pay out anything until they have received the certificate from the Department of Railways and Canals that the money has been expended by the railways in accordance with the vote. Our officers go to the head office, or wherever it is necessary for them to go to make the audit, and on their report the Finance Minister issues the cheque.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Do I understand the minister to mean that the board in Toronto cannot expend any money without the minister authorizing that expenditure?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: They can expend all the earnings without any certificate from the Railway Department, but they cannot get any money from the Finance Department until they get a certificate from the Railway Department that the work is necessary. Then the money is provided as the work proceeds.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: If I understand the minister rightly, there is this distinction to be drawn. The board in Toronto has the right to expend all the receipts of the railways, but thqy cannot expend any money in excess of those receipts until the expenditure has been authorized by the Government.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: They have to get a certificate from the Railway Department.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Then this year, with a .deficit of $70,000,000, the minister authorized the expenditure of every cent of that $70,000,000?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Of course, we must authorize it. If the receipts are not sufficient, our auditor must go out and audit the amount over and above the earnings before the board can get any money from the Finance Department.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
That is the money is expended and the accounts are audited afterwards? Am I to understand that there is no official in the Department of Railways, not even the minister himself, with any authority to control the expenditure, and that the only thing the Railway Department does is to send out its auditor

and then the Government pays to the railways whatever amount the auditor finds has been expended in excess of the receipts?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: That is right. None of the officials or the minister has anything to do with the expenditure. That is left entirely to the management.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Suppose there was gross mismanagement. In the face of evidence of such mismanagement has the minister no authority, or has no official in his department authority, to stop that mismanagement? Can the board continue to squander the money without the minister being able to interfere?	[DOT]

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: The hon. member must understand that if any case of mismanagement or wrong-doing is brought to the attention of the Government, we could put an end to the management at any time, but we have had nothing of that kind brought to our attention.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Does the minister maintain that even though the returns this year show such an enormous deficit, and even though the accounts are audited by his officials every week or every month, whichever it is, there is nothing wrong with the management, and that he has never interfered with the Board? Am I to understand that he has never interfered on any occasion at all?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
I have not yet had
brought to my attention any case of wrongdoing so far as the railways are concerned; neither have I had any case of mismanagement brought to my attention. The fact that there is a deficit of $70,000,000 does not mean that there has been any wrongdoing. If it did, then every manager of a railway in the United States should be dismissed, because their railways show deficits. A deficit does not imply wrongdoing or even mismanagement.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
I am not talking about
wrong-doing; I simply used the word mismanagement. Does the minister say that though he observed this deficit piling up every month he never interfered? Did he think everything was all right all through the year?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
We have a board of
management operating the Canadian National railways. They were placed in charge, and have been operating the railway. I have not in any way interfered with them. I feel that if the operation of
the Canadian National railways is to be made a success, as I hope it will, there must be no interference by the Minister of Railways or any other member of the Government. That is the position I take.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I do not say that I disagree with the minister, although I think his experience might be very useful even to the board. Perhaps the minister is really too modest when he says he should not interfere. Sometimes interference might be effective. If the management of the Canadian National railways is exclusively under the board, why have a minister of railways at all? Let the hon. gentleman be minister of canals, or of any other department, because it would be a pity for him to leave the Cabinet; but why have a minister of railways when he has absolutely nothing to do with our railways? And there is a personal consideration in the matter. I do not see why the hon. gentleman should shoulder the responsibility for our railway situation and be held accountable throughout Canada for present conditions if, in fact, he has nothing to do with them. Why should he persist in keeping this portfolio when he has no authority whatever? I think he should change the name of his department, and restrict his activities to the canals of the country; the blame for the railway situation should certainly not rest on his shoulders if he asures lis that he has nothing to do with the railways. In any event, what has he to do? I think that is a fair question, and it calls for a fair answer. This is an important matter, and I will repeat the question: Why have we a minister of railways? The minister does not answer, but I should like him to justify his retention of the title "Minister of Railways." When am I to receive an answer to this question?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Next sitting of the House.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
What are the duties of
the Minister of Railways?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I have explained that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
The minister explained
it by saying that most of the work done by his department consisted in correspondence. Well, I am sure that the hon. gentleman does not do the correspondence himself, and I think that the committee ought to be told exactly what the powers and duties of the Minister of Railways are. The hon. gentleman said plainly a moment ago that he had nothing to do with the railways, and has never interfered with their administration.

Then, if the Minister of Railways has nothing to do with railways, what on earth is he doing?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Question.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I do not wish to interrupt the minister if he is about to reply to the hon. member. If not, I want to ask another question. Returning to the matter of highways, the minister says he has a numerous list of engineers and others employed, because of service in connection with the highways. I take it for granted that it is understood the arrangements between the Dominion Government and the provinces are to continue for the present year?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Yes. The hon. member will recall that the Act provided a period of five years; the arrangement is being carried on this year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: So far as the Dominion Government is concerned, it is intended to continue the same system?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
Yes; the agreements
were and are being made. We must pay our forty per cent so long as the Provincial Governments continue the work.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Will the minister answer my question?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
I do not wish to be
discourteous, but I cannot give any other answer than I have already given.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: No occupation.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Is the minister content to remain in well paid inactivity, as Mr. Winston Churchill says?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I want some light in regard to the directors. Do I understand that these men are directors of the Canadian Northern railway only?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: And of the subsidiary companies also.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: But not of the Intercolonial, the Transcontinental, or the National railways?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
No, because they are
not a corporate company. They are owned entirely by the Government. The direction of these roads is under the management of the Canadian National railways.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: They are directors of the Canadian National Railways Company?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
No, of the Canadian
Northern.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Are there no directors for the Canadian National Railway Company?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
That Bill has not yet
been brought into effect.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: There is no such company as the Canadian National Railway Company?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: That is only a descriptive title. We passed an Order in Council providing that the title "Canadian National Railways" should be used until we brought into force the Act passed two years ago.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I understand that the term "Canadian National Railways" is descriptive of-

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Mr. Chairman, I have been attempting to speak pretty often and so far I have not succeeded in getting the floor. Now I am going to stand up until I get what information I want. I think it is about time that the Minister of Railways and Canals had a few minutes' rest.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Hear, hear.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Now, I have not very many complaints to make; I made them before the Government bought these railways. I had the courage to get up and warn them what was coming. I told them it was going to be a knock-out blow to. the country, but they did not believe me. I told them that it would involve a debt not only on the present generation, but on unborn generations, and my words are now proving pretty nearly true. Not only have we not got the debt approximately discharged, but generations to come will be shouldered with a great burden. We have two lines of the Canadian Northern running through my country, as well as a canal, and I think there are sufficient employees on those two railways and the canal to win the next general election for the Union Government.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: That is encouraging.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
They have been making improvements from time to time, and whenever any work is needed to be done a good old Tory gets the job. Two bridges were built in that constituency about ten years ago, and the engineers at that time said they were going to build structures that would be strong enough to stand for all time. Now what do we find? Last year these splendid bridges were pulled down

and clumsy, cumbersome things put in their place,-bridges that have no strength whatever. What farmer, if he had; ia waggon that was not strong enough for his purposes, would, instead of fixing the wheels and axles, make an enormous body that would carry millions of tons?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Oh, oh.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
Well, the comparison is not so far fetched after all, in view of the nature of these bridges. I say, what farmer would neglect the wheels and axles and build a disproportionate body for his waggon? That is just the case in connection with these bridges. They are tremendous structures capable of bearing a heavier weight than a passing train, but they are placed on weak abutments. I am not an engineer, but I have common sense, and, in my opinion at least, these bridges are not as strong as they were before. It provides work, and the people are employed from one end of the country to the other-they all get jobs. However, I do not know where the money is coming from.
I think it would be well for the Minister of Railways with such a big expenditure going on in the county which I represent to take a run down there and size things up for himself. I would be satisfied with his judgment if he would say that this bridge was good for a number of years yet until we get out of debt. Leave it alone for the present; it will carry us all right. But we never find the minister going down there and looking into these things, he leaves matters to the managing committee that is putting the country to such expense from day to day until such a situation is reached that the chances are ten to one if we will ever get out of it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I wish to ask the minister a question in connection with these directors. I understand that these gentlemen are directors of the Canadian Northern and its subsidiary companies-

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: There was a ruling given by the Chair earlier in the evening that a discussion of such matters is at present quite out of order.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Matters of what kind?

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Any discussion relating to the item under consideration will of course be quite in order. The item relates to detail of civil government.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I understand that the Deputy Minister of Railways is a director of the Management Board-is that your understanding, Mr. Chairman?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I might say that-

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I was asking the Chairman for his ruling.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: The ruling of the Chair was that discussion of any matters connected with the Outside Service of the railway was quite out of order. Only discussion upon matters pertaining to the vote we are now considering is relevant.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Am I to understand that discussion pertaining to outside matters is relevant?

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
If the hon. gentleman did not grasp what I said I will repeat it.
I say that discussion of matters pertaining to the Outside Service is not in order.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Will the Chairman tell me whether the deputy minister would be regarded as belonging to the Outside or the Inside Service? I see that he is a member of the Board of Directors of the Canadian National Railways, and I would therefore like to know if he is to be regarded in the Outside or the Inside Service?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I would have to explain that. The deputy minister's salary as such is included in the item under civil government. His position as a director comes under another item, but of course I am willing to give the hon. member any reasonable information he wants. I have no objection to enlarging the field and discussing this or any other item, but the Chairman has ruled that the discussion must be limited to the item we are now considering. If we pass this vote the next item will enable hon. members to talk upon the activities of any branch of the railway system.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: What does the minister mean by the next item?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I mean that upon the next item we will take up you could discuss any question in connection with the railways system. I am not raising any objection to the present discussion, except that I think perhaps it would be well to adhere to the ruling that has been given.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
I am quite satisfied, Mr. Chairman, to abide by your ruling but I want you to carve the deputy minister and tell me just what portion of him belongs to the Outside Service and what portion to the Inside Service? Then I can follow your ruling and not render myself liable to be called to order. I have no desire

whatever to dispute your ruling; in fact, I wish to follow it. I now wish to know whether the deputy minister, and the other directors of the Canadian National system appoint the management for the Government railways, or whether they are appointed by the Minister of Railways?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: That is a question I will have to answer myself, and the Chairman can then give such ruling as the case seems to call for. The question has been asked whether the deputy minister comes under this item. He is paid a salary as deputy minister in the Inside Service and that is included in this item. Then as a director he gets a certain amount but that appears in another item altogether.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: He gets a certain amount beside his salary?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Yes, besides his salary. In the item we are now considering, the amount the deputy minister receives as a director is not included. When we come to the next item hon. members may ask any question they please about the deputy minister or any other of the other directors.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: With your permission, Mr. Chairman, I wish to know what the minister means by "another item." I did not have any idea that we were to go on with any of the Estimates of the Department of Railways to-night. In view of the explanation given by the Prime Minister that a committee was to be appointed to deal with the railways I understood the Miniser of Railways would take up only the items relating to Civil Government. 1 now ask if it is the intention of the minister to go on with any other item.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: What I meant was, that if we passed the item relating to Civil Government and proposed to take up another item I would not see any harm in doing so. Then hon. gentlemen could discuss any matters in connection with the operation of our railways. If we remain in committee on the items of Civil Government then the ruling of the Chair must be borne in mind. I am not urging that the next item should be passed if we do go on, but I would then be in a position to give the committee information that was asked for with respect to any item that might happen to be discussed.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: What is covered by the item "Sundries, $10,000?"

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
My deputy tells me that aplies to incidental expenses in con-

nection with the department. [DOT] He is now getting the details and they will be available in a moment.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: While waiting for those details I would like to again refer to the matter of the salary of the deputy minister. The minister has informed us that the deputy minister is also a director of the Canadian National Railways. I do not think that this is good policy or that it is a all in consonance with the principles of good organization. We are asked to vote this gentleman a salary as deputy minister, and the same official will go to Toronto and sit on the Board of directors and be independent of his own boss. How can we reconcile the two positions? I do not wish to attack the deputy minister, I am sure that he is a good official, but I say that he cannot satisfactorily hold the two positions at the one time. Let him be Deputy Minister of Railways and draw his salary as such, or if he prefers to be a director of the Canadian Na tional Railways let him be that; but he cannot be both. Earlier in the evening the minister explained that all moneys expended by the Canadian National Railways are checked up by the department. Naturally one of those who sees to the very close checking up of those accounts would be the deputy minister, and if on the one hand he is paid to protect his department, on the other hand he is paid also to go to Toronto to spend the department's money, I do not think this anomaly ought to continue any longer. I do not see the reason why Mr. Bell, after being appointed a director, remains deputy minister. I would like the minister to give the committee an explanation on this point and say whether the arrangement works out well. I do not see how it possibly can. How can the deputy minister, after attending to his departmental duties, go to Toronto and act as a director absolutely independent of his minister?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
The deputy minister
gets the usual director's fees. The other directors receive $2,000 each, and there is no reason why he should not receive that amount as well. As I stated a few minutes ago, a large amount of money that is voted by this House on account of the National Railways must be certified to by the board of directors. I think it is a good idea to have an official of the department at the directors' meetings to see that the moneys are properly expended and give any explanations that are necessary.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: The moment the deputy head of the minister's department sits on the Board of Directors, and a decision is taken by that board in which the deputy minister concurs, the department is bound. If that decision is not in the best interests of the country how could the department move to have it changed if the deputy minister as director has concurred in it and has shared in the expenditure? The hon. minister had not considered that apparently when answering me a minute ago. To sum up my objection,-the deputy minister represents the department at the board; therefore the department is a party to all decisions taken; and if bad decisions are taken and money is expended which should not be expended, the department is bound by those decisions and cannot exercise a proper checking up of the expenditure.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
Of course, the hon.
member knows that a decision of the board would be final any way, but the deputy minister being on the board would not agree unless they were carrying out exactly what was intended by Parliament. If by any chance that board should do something other than what Parliament had authorized, of course, the deputy minister would inform the minister of the Government on his return, and the mistake could be corrected. I think it is a great advantage to have him on the board.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Has the deputy minister ever disagreed with the decisions of the board?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: If he disagreed the board would do what was right, because they would not want him to report and recommend the Government to take action. The board might innocently take some action not in accordance with what should be done, and having the deputy minister present he would be able to give them information and advice and see that what Parliament authorized was properly carried out. If he made a report that the board had passed some resolution not in accordance with what Parliament had authorized, I think that some action would be at once taken by the Government.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I do not understand the minister very clearly. At first he told us that decisions taken by the board were final. If such is the case, how could the deputy minister have them changed?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: The hon. member knows that the actions of the Board of Directors are supposed to be final, and are final unless they are not in accordance with what Parliament has authorized. Now, I say that if the deputy minister reported next day that such irregular action had been taken, the Government would have power to remove the directors. I am satisfied that the presence of the deputy minister to give advice and point out the intention of Parliament is of great assistance to the directors, and I have no doubt they would follow his advice.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: How often does the Board of Directors meet?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: The Board of Directors have a regular meeting once a month. Of course, they may have special meetings now and again.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
Dui^ng 1920 how
many special meetings were held besides the regular meetings?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I have not that information now, but I will get it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Are regular minutes of the Board of Directors kept?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Yes, by the Board of Directors in Toronto.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Will those minutes show the attendance of the directors at the meetings?

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
Order. The hon.
member for Brome (Mr. McMaster) perhaps was not in the House when this item was first reached, and the ruling was given that anything relating to the Board of Directors of the Canadian National Railways could be properly asked only on the item providing the expenditure incurred by that board, which, I hope, will be reached during the evening. The discussion which was brought up by the hon. member for Dorchester was of course more relevant because it related to the position of the deputy minister upon that board, and for that reason was allowed.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
I think it would be
proper to ask the minister to ask the deputy minister how often the board met.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
That question was
allowed.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I said to the hon. member that I did not have that information, but that I would have it at the next sitting.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
I asked the minister
a question a while ago with regard to the item of sundries. We cannot hear very well

at this end of the chamber, and I did not' catch his reply.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
The amount is for
temporary assistants and various small items, typewriters and things of that kind-small supplies.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
There ,is another
item here for $13,000 covering printing and stationery. It seems to me that $10,000 is a pretty large item for sundries. If a man included in his statement of election expenses an amount of $10,000 for sundries, his statement would be questioned. The item appears to me to be too large to be allowed to pass without our having some information as to what it is intended for.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
Is there a gentleman
named Hayter ip the Department of Railways and Canals?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
He is in the Auditor
General's Department. I think he is the official who has Charge of the railway accounting in that department. He has never been paid as an official of the Railway Department.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Who is Mr. Cope? Is he in the Railway Department?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
When Mr. Bell was
promoted to the position of deputy minister, Mr. Cope took his place as financial comptroller of the department.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
At page W-234 of the
Auditor General's report, volume 3, 1920,
I find some correspondence on the subject of the audit. I find that Mr. Hayter asks for permission to audit the Canadian National accounts, and the correspondence apparently concludes with a letter from G. A. Bell to the effect that all the cheques, vouchers and other documents relative to expenditure made by the Government railway under vote number 96 will be supplied to any person having authority to call for them. I would like to know what "Government railway" means in that connection.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
The Intercolonial and
the Transcontinental.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
The letter refers first
to the Canadian National railways and afterwards to the Government railways.
It would seem to be misleading in that respect.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
It says:
I have been advised by the treasurer of Canadian National Railways that all the

cheques, vouchers and other documents relative to expenditure made by the Government railway-
And so on. The Intercolonial and the Transcontinental have been known as the Government railways.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Under what item do we find the appropriation for the salaries of the managers of the Canadian National Railways?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Mr. Hanna and his staff are paid out of the total earnings of the whole system-that is, the several railways that go to make up the Canadian National Railway system. There is apportioned to each part of the system its share of these salaries.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: That cannot be, because there is a separate company there, the Canadian Northern. They employ certain gentlemen and the minister, in tu!rn, employs certain gentlemen for the purposes of management; in this case they happen to be the same persons. Where is the vote for the payment of these men? The expenditure must be submitted to the Auditor General, unless you are cutting corners.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: The salaries of Mr. Hanna and his officials do not appear in the Auditor General's report. The report laid on the table of the House gives the total revenue and the total expenditure of all these railways, but the details are not at hand just at the moment. However, I will give the information to the House when we come to the particular item concerned, and as it is asked for.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Well, it is being asked for now.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: It does not come under this item.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: That may be so, but we are voting the salaries of Civil Government employees in connection with the management of the Government Railways. As I understand it, the Government railways stand in the same position as the Canadian National; they did not change their status in any particular. That is, they bear the same relation to the Government and the people of Canada as they did before, except that the minister employs the same management as he has for the Canadian Northern system.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
Mr. Hayes was the manager of the Intercolonial before the Canadian Northern was taken over, and the Transcontinental was under Mr. APRIL 6, 1921
Brady. Both these managers reported direct to the Government. They resigned these positions when the other railways were taken over and assumed other duties in connection with the Canadian National Railway system. Then we appointed the hoard of Directors of the Canadian Northern,-what we now call the Canadian National,-as managers also of the Intercolonial and the Transcontinental, and the management was therefore taken over entirely by these gentlemen. Of course, the salaries and expenses in connection with the Canadian Northern system,-what we call the Canadian National system,-are all paid at Toronto and the details kept there. Any information the hon. gentleman wants, I can give to the committee in connection with any of these expenditures. If the hon. gentleman lets me know a little time ahead what information he wants, I can have it ready for him when I am on my Estimates again; or when I am on my Estimates, if he lets me know the information he wants, I can get it for him.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: The other night the minister seemed to be under a sort of eclipse and no information was available. I am delighted to hear him say to-night that he is going to give any information that may be required. He told us this evening that the Canadian National Railway Company, the Bill for which was forced through this House, was never brought into operation. Therefore, there is no such thing as the Canadian National Railway Company; it is not a company; it has no standing, and it is not in a position to hire people and pay them, because it has no funds. Therefore, the employees, the civil servants in connection with the Canadian Government Railways, must be paid by some person. If that does not appear in this item, I should like to know where it appears.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
It appears in item 126, for a loan not exceeding $50,000,000, which may be used "to meet expenditures made or indebtedness incurred at any time by or on behalf of the Canadian Northern Railway Company, the Canadian National Railway Company, or any company comprised in the Canadian Northern Railway system." If the hon. member will also look at item 341, he will find an appropriation there of $7,000,000 towards any deficiency in receipts and revenues necessary to meet working expenditures on the Canadian Government railways. He will see that there are two separate items, and his question would, of
course, be in order when those items come up.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: The minister stated that there was no such thing as the Canadian National. The Canadian Northern is a different proposition. We have a Canadian Government railway.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I cannot answer for the minister; I can speak only for the Chair. The ruling of the Chair is that the question and the discussion in answer to the question put by the hon. member are out of order at this stage.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Some time ago, in answer to the hon. member for Dorchester (Mr. Cannon), the minister made it quite clear that it was no part of his functions' to interfere in the management of the Government roads. He also wished the hon. mefti-ber for Dorchester to state whether he referred to cases of dishonesty or fraud. Would the minister interfere if he had brought to his attention a case of fraud or malpractice on the part of an employee on the Canadian National railways in the discharge of his duty?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Matters of that kind have been brought to my attention, and I have immediately brought them to the attention of the Board of Management and they have always taken action. I would be very much surprised if, when a case of that kind was brought to their attention, they should not take action.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I asked that because complaints have been made to me with reference to one such case in which the directors would not take action.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I certainly cannot allow the hon. member to go into that case on this item.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I am not going into it.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: It will have to came up under item 126 or item 341.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I do not wish to offend the Chairman in any way, but I would ask him to call me out of order when I am out of order. I was not going into this matter; I was asking the minister if I could bring such cases to his attention.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I will say that the hon. gentleman is out of order in asking the question.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
I am quite satisfied that the Chairman can call me out of order whenever he likes, and he knows that. But

I am asking when I might bring this matter to the attention of the minister, and I do not see that there is any occasion for heat on the part of the Chairman of the committee. I understand, in answer to some question by the member for Dorchester, the minister stated that a reason for a decrease in this item was that Mr. Mon-sarrat had left the employ of the Government. Who has replaced Mr. Monsar-rat.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: We have abolished that position.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Who controls the Quebec bridge ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: The Board of Directors of the Canadian National Railways.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Has the minister a purchasing agent in the department at Ottawa?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
We have an agent
here, but he does not make the purchases direct as was done heretofore. Mr. Lavoie used to make the purchases before the Intercolonial and the Transcontinental came under the Canadian National Railway system. Mr. Lavoie was removed to Toronto. We have at Ottawa one or two men who prepare requisitions and attend to arranging items, and then the Purchasing Commission makes the purchases.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
I notice in this item there
is so much for an assistant purchasing agent and so much for a junior purchasing agent, but nothing for a purchasing agent.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
I explained a little
while ago that the Civil Service Commission gave those men those titles. They were employed here as assistants under Mr. Lavoie who had quite a little staff when he was in the department. We had to keep those officials in the department to carry out the work in connection with getting requisitions ready for the Purchasing Commission.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: What work do the assistant purchasing agent and the junior purchasing agent do? Is it in connection with the Government at Ottawa or in connection with purchasing for Government railways generally?	-

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Only purchases in connection with the canals. They have nothing to do with the railways in any shape or form. The purchases for the Intercolonial, Transcontinental, Canadian Northern and all those systems is done through Mr. Lavoie, the purchasing agent at Toronto.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: In purchasing for the canals, do the assistant and junior purchasing agents have full authority, or do they just report to the minister?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: They have no authority to purchase at all. The purchases are made now by the Purchasing Commission which purchases for the several departments of the Government.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
Are they members of that
commission?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: No.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
What are they here for if
they have nothing to do?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: They prepare specifications and requisitions. There is a good deal of work in connection with getting specifications and all that sort of thing ready before tenders are called.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I see an item in regard to four travelling auditors.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I explained that a few minutes ago, but I do not object to giving the explanation again. These men have been in the department for some time. They have a great deal of work to do. They1 were there when we had the Intercolonial and Transcontinental, and since those roads have been handed over to the management, the highways work has been transferred to our department. All the expenditures in connection with that work made by the different provinces have to be checked up by our auditors. Then they have the canal work as well. We alpo have to send them to Toronto to audit the expenditures that have been voted by the House. So they are fully employed.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Since the department is no longer managing our railways, what is the object of retaining a right-of-way agent?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: He is busy all the time in connection with the canals. Then there is purchasing to be done in connection with other works. Leases, for instance, are being granted almost daily for properties along the canal. I may add that this man used to do work in connection with the Intercolonial. He is a splendid man, a first-class man, and for that reason we have loaned him to other departments, the Public Works Department, for instance.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
I am not making any
objections to the man at all. I do not know whether he is a first-class man or a third-class man, but I cannot understand why

we should be passing this item for the Department of Railways and Canals when there is really no work pertaining to the railways for this man to do. If his work pertains solely to the canals, why not say so, and let us dispense with this discussion when the Railway Estimates are being considered. I understood that these Estimates pertained to both the railways and canals, but apparently all these officials whose salaries we are voting are doing canal work only, since the Government have washed their hands of the railways. Is the deputy minister considered as the deputy minister of Canals here or as the deputy minister of railways?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: He is Deputy Minister of Railways and Canals.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: What are his functions as Deputy Minister of Railways?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: He has a lot to do in connection with the items we are passing. We are voting very large expenditures in connection with the Canadian Northern and the Grand Trunk, and the deputy minister is responsible for the work in connection with these items.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
That would be in his
capacity as director of the Canadian National Railways?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: No, as deputy minister.	-

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
