speechtext: Why do we need a comptroller and a secretary and the rest of these gentlemen, now the railways have been transferred to the company?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
The comptroller has
charge of the expenditure. There is a comptroller in every large spending department.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I see there are three "secretaries to executive". Who is the executive?	'

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: There are three secretaries, one for the deputy minister, one for the chief engineer, and one for the comptroller.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
And the minister also has a secretary?
Hon. Mr, REID:	Oh, yes. The Civil
Service Commission has given this title to the secretaries of the three officials I have mentioned.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
It seems extraordinary that the comptroller, for instance, should
be designated an executive. I understood the executive of a department to be exclusively the head of the department.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: What are the duties of the bridge and structural engineer?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: That was Mr. Mont-sarrat. When the Quebec bridge was completed, it was decided to keep Mr. Montsar-rat on for a year or two, in order to see that that work was all right. We kept him on, and two or three other gentlemen, and that was the title he had. He retired from the department on March 31.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Has he been transferred to the company?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: No, he has gone into private practice.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: We are asked to vote $202,000 for salaries, and $28,000 for contingencies, for the Department of Railways and Canals. The salaries are to be paid to ninety-five officials. It seems to me that as they cannot have the work to do that they had before the railways were transferred to the so-called company with headquarters in Toronto, there should be a reduction in the staff, unless the minister can show the committee that there is as much work to do in the department now as there was four or five years ago. The country certainly cannot understand why there should be as many officials in the department now as there were before the railways were transferred. I can understand that the minister is not in a position to give me the information to-night, but I should like him to tell the committee when his Estimates are up again, how many officials were employed in connection with this item under Civil Government in 191415, or, say, the year before the railways were transferred to the company.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I shall be very glad to get that information. I may say to the hon. member that we made a reduction in the staff last year. I might also say that the highways work has been transferred to the department, which means the addition of a few more officials, at least.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I see that the head statistical cjerk has been eliminated from this year's vote. Is there a statistical branch in the department now?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Mr. Payne was head statistical clerk, but he has been retired from the Government service.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
Is there no statistical
branch in the department of railways now? Is there no statistical branch available to the Canadian people in any department at the present time?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Oh, yes. About one or two years ago a Bill was passed transferring the statistical work of all departments to the Department of Trade and Commerce, and providing that a report should be laid on the Table every year showing the statistics for each department. The Board of Railway Commissioners also keeps statistics.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I see that there is an official here called a records searcher. Am I to understand that the records are lost in the department and that he is supposed to search after them?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: We have one man, Mr. Ross, who has been in the department many years doing this work of turning up records as they are wanted. A great many applications are made by the public for documents, and this gentleman, who has been engaged in this work for a long time, hunts them up.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Would it not be better to call this official "Keeper of Records"? Was the present title given by the commission?

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
I wish the minister
would have more control over the commission.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: So do I; I should be glad to.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: Any man who looked at the list and saw that this gentleman was a record searcher would naturally be under the impression that records were lost for which he had to search. If he keeps records, let him be designated accordingly. I see that most of the titles ascribed by the Civil Service Commission are quite inappropriate. It would be better for the minister to have proper titles for his officials so that people might know exactly what they were doing.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I agree with the hon. gentleman. I have not been entirely satisfied with some of the titles given by the Civil Service Commission, but they have power in the matter.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
I should like some information in regard to Mr. H. Forman, who appears at page "234-W" of the Auditor General's Report.
[Mr J. I). Reid.]	.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: He is treasurer in Toronto. I will have information in regard to hipi when we come to the next item.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: The Minister of Railways has told us that he has no control over the Board of Directors. He has said on two or three different occasions that the deputy minister attends meetings of the Board of Directors, and may exercise certain control over their deliberations. Does the deputy act under the direction of the minister? If he does, we can establish the connection and show that the minister in an indirect way, through the deputy minister, has control over the Board of Directors.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: I must answer, "no."

Item agreed to.
Progress reported.
On the motion of Right Hon. Mr. Doherty for the adjournment of the House:

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: What will be the business to-morrow?

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: We expect to take up the Estimates of the Department of Marine and Naval Affairs, and of Railways, and the motion for the appointment of a committee in connection with railway operations.

maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext: That is a motion of which we require longer notice. I will not press my objection at the moment, but it really requires two days' notice.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: SUPPLY-MINISTER OF LABOUR AND THE NATIONAL CATHOLIC LABOUR UNIONS
speechtext:
If it is not ripe for action, it will riot be taken up.
Motion agreed to and the House adjourned at 11.20 p.m.
Thursday!, April 7, 1921
